overview: The largest text component in the type system, reserved for high-impact, oversized text. Use it for hero moments, key metrics, feature callouts, or prominent identifiers where maximum visual weight is needed. Sits above Heading in the typographic scale.

whenToUse: For large hero or landing-page headlines that need maximum visual impact above the fold
When a typographic centrepiece is needed for a marketing-style section or splash view
do: Use size 1 for the primary display headline and size 2 for a secondary or sub-display line beneath it
Use the branded variant when the headline should carry the product's primary color identity
Test legibility at smaller breakpoints — display text is very large and may need adjustment at mobile sizes
dont: Don't use display text for section headings or body copy — it's purely large-scale decorative typography; use Headings instead
Don't place more than one display headline in a single view; it dilutes the visual impact of each
Don't use the branded variant when the surrounding palette already supplies strong color — it can create excessive contrast
